mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the current month
regime_hint: FED Funds rate above 4% in late-cycle tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (p > 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS relative to INDPRO indicates strengthening labor market demand, which is associated with higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investor confidence improves.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS/INDPRO ratio increases by more than 5% over the past 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with PAYEMS/INDPRO ratio change (R² < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in HOUST (units of new orders) followed by a rebound above the prior month's level predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as a sign of improving business demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST drops for two consecutive months then rises in the third month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative during the identified rebound period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) of over 2% is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as market anticipates weaker earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly value falls by >2% from the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction quarter.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to lower real interest rates boosting equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior month's average (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and RSAFS (employment and retail sales) above their prior month's levels suggests economic momentum, predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: Both PAYEMS and RSAFS increase by at least 3% from previous month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined proxy change (R² < 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL inflation above 3%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to expectations of rate hikes dampening growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the inflation period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) followed by a failure to recover in the next two months predicts a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as a signal of weak manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >10% in a month and remains below prior month's value for two months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the failure to recover period.
